newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas falls in summer on Ofgas tender decision.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas falls in summer on Ofgas tender decision.

text.p: U.K. spot natural gas prices softened in the summer on Tuesday afternoon, with August and September bearing the brunt of the weakness, traders and brokers said.
August and September came off following the decision by Ofgas to accept Network Code modification 157, proposed by Enron Corp.

This allows Transco to sell gas from its summer storage gas tender at the NBP as well as in storage. And Ofgas has recommended to Transco that it sells the gas in August and September, with the result that there is effectively a significant increase in the volume of spot gas available in those months.

"It's been very much a wait and see day," said a trader, adding that few players were willing to take positions ahead of the Ofgas decision on the storage tender. But the mood on the market was bearish, with most expecting that sales at the NBP were going to be allowed.

Otherwise there was continued interest for prompt gas, especially day ahead material, at prices between 10.70 pence and 11.20 pence a therm. Recent system buying on the flexibility mechanism has kept the system average price high and is seen as responsible for the continued strong levels on the prompt market, dealers said.
Price levels in the winter were steadier, although some traders believe the weakness in August and September will eventually filter through to the fourth quarter and perhaps beyond.
But so far this has not been seen, and Q4 was traded at 12.325 pence a therm on Tuesday, in line with Monday's levels.

And the Q4/Q1 strip traded at both 14.15 pence and 14.10 pence a therm, both higher levels than seen on Monday. But in general activity was subdued, with players citing waiting for the Ofgas decision as the factor slowing down trade.
